title: Health profiling through cross-session analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions to perform health-condition analysis. This enables profiling of individuals based on their health data patterns, linking data points to create comprehensive health profiles.
assumptions: Health logs contain sufficient data points across sessions to enable meaningful profiling

title: Quasi-identifier identification through health patterns
description: Health data (calorie intake, weight, exercise patterns) across sessions can serve as quasi-identifiers that uniquely identify individuals, especially when combined with temporal patterns.
assumptions: Health data patterns are sufficiently unique to identify individuals

title: Sensitive health data collection
description: Health logs containing calorie, weight, and exercise data are highly sensitive personal data types. Processing this data for health-condition analysis requires careful justification of necessity.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Excessive volume of health data processing
description: Reading health logs 'across sessions' suggests processing of historical data beyond what may be functionally necessary for current health-condition analysis, potentially violating data minimization.
assumptions: Not all historical session data is required for the stated analytical purpose
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether all historical data is functionally necessary

title: Unawareness of health data analysis
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across sessions for health-condition analysis, beyond basic storage and retrieval.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about cross-session health analytics

title: Lack of control over health data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is analyzed for health-condition purposes.
assumptions: No user preference mechanism exists for health analytics processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health logs across all sessions for health-condition analysis may process more personal data than is actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this health data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific functional requirements of the health analysis

title: Lawfulness concerns for sensitive health data processing
description: Health data is special category data under GDPR requiring specific lawful grounds. Processing for health-condition analysis may require explicit consent or other specific legal basis.
assumptions: GDPR applies and health data qualifies as special category data
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific legal basis established for this processing

title: Sensitive health data types disclosed
description: Health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags are highly sensitive personal data types that may exceed what is functionally required for the app's operation.
assumptions: Health analytics data is considered sensitive under most privacy frameworks

title: Unnecessary data enrichment and analysis
description: The analytics service performs inference and enrichment on health data to generate risk indicators and trend flags, which may go beyond what is necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: Inferred insights involve additional processing beyond raw data transmission

title: Individual profiling through health analytics
description: Health analytics service creates profiles of individuals based on their health data, enabling linking of various data points to specific individuals through pattern analysis.
assumptions: Analytics service performs individual-level analysis to generate insights

title: Revealing health attributes enable identification
description: Health-condition risk indicators and routine summaries contain revealing attributes that could support identification of data subjects, especially when combined with other data.
assumptions: Health insights contain attributes that could be used to identify individuals

title: Users unaware of health insight processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health data is being analyzed to generate risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that are then returned to the app.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into what analytics are performed on their health data

title: Lack of user control over health analytics preferences
description: Users may lack control over what types of health insights are generated, how they are processed, and whether they want to receive certain types of risk indicators or trend flags.
assumptions: App may not provide granular controls over analytics processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing and returning inferred health insights (risk indicators, trend flags) may involve more personal data processing than is actually needed for the app's functionality.
assumptions: GDPR or similar privacy regulations apply to health data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory context and functional requirements

title: Lawfulness concerns for automated health decision-making
description: Automated generation of health-condition risk indicators may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data, requiring specific legal grounds and safeguards.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive/special category data under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether risk indicators constitute automated decisions with legal effects

title: Sensitive health data disclosure
description: The app displays inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, which are highly sensitive health data types. This disclosure may exceed what is functionally necessary for the user to understand their health status, especially if the inference methodology is not transparent or if the granularity of risk indicators is more detailed than needed.
assumptions: The inferred condition indicators are considered sensitive personal data under health privacy regulations

title: Excessive data granularity in health indicators
description: The app displays trends and inferred condition indicators with potentially fine-grained detail about eating-disorder or diabetes risk. This level of granularity may be more detailed than functionally required for the user to take appropriate action.
assumptions: The risk signals include detailed trend information beyond basic status indicators

title: User unawareness of inference processing
description: The user may not be fully aware that the app is performing inference to derive eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals from their data. The processing of data to generate these health indicators may not be transparent to the user.
assumptions: The inference methodology and data sources used for risk calculation are not clearly communicated to users

title: Lack of user control over health indicator display
description: The user may lack control over whether and how inferred health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) are displayed. They may not be able to customize or opt out of receiving these sensitive inferences.
assumptions: The app does not provide granular preferences for controlling health indicator display

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Displaying inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals may process more personal data than necessary. The inference and display of these sensitive health indicators should be strictly limited to what is functionally required.
assumptions: The health risk indicators may include more data than minimally necessary for user benefit

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: The app performs automated inference to generate eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, which constitutes automated decision making on sensitive personal data. This may require specific legal grounds and safeguards under GDPR and similar regulations.
assumptions: The inference process constitutes automated decision making under applicable privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific regulatory interpretation of automated health risk inference

title: Highly sensitive health data disclosed to third-party cloud provider
description: The full health and location dataset is being hosted and replicated at a third-party cloud provider. Health data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly necessary and with appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive personal data under most privacy regulations

title: Excessive volume of personal data processed
description: The 'full health and location dataset' is being transferred and stored at the cloud provider, which may include more data than functionally necessary for analytics purposes.
assumptions: The term 'full dataset' suggests comprehensive data transfer rather than minimized data

title: Personal data exposed to predetermined external party
description: Health and location data is made accessible to the cloud hosting provider (EE2), an external party. While predetermined, this still represents data exposure beyond the original system boundary.
assumptions: Cloud provider is a known third-party service

title: Quasi-identifiers in health and location data
description: The combination of health data and location data can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow re-identification of individuals even if direct identifiers are removed.
assumptions: Health and location data combined can uniquely identify individuals

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Health and location data can be combined to create quasi-identifiers that enable linking of data to specific individuals across different datasets or contexts.
assumptions: Location and health data together form strong quasi-identifiers

title: Data subjects unaware of cloud provider data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health and location data is being transferred to and stored at a third-party cloud hosting provider.
assumptions: Data subjects may not have been informed about third-party cloud hosting

title: Lack of control over data rectification and erasure at cloud provider
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify or erase their personal data that is hosted and replicated at the third-party cloud provider.
assumptions: Cloud provider data management may not support direct data subject rights

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Transferring the 'full health and location dataset' to a cloud provider may violate the data minimization principle if not all data is necessary for the analytics functionality.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to health data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether all data is actually necessary for analytics

title: Lawfulness concerns for health data processing
description: Health data is special category data requiring specific lawful grounds for processing. Third-party cloud hosting may complicate compliance with these requirements.
assumptions: Health data qualifies as special category/sensitive data under applicable regulations
